subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: What filesystem permission boundary should OpenClaw expose for agent-created user-facing output files on shared hosts?
rationale: The implementation would add config surface and intentionally change local file access semantics across multiple write paths, so automation cannot choose the security/product tradeoff safely.

options.title: Scoped opt-in policy
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped user-output permission policy that applies only to approved agent-output paths and explicitly excludes OpenClaw private state.

options.title: Narrow fixed defaults
options.body: Set conventional modes on a small set of user-facing writers, but accept that exec, sandbox, and plugin output may remain inconsistent.

options.title: Document external ownership
options.body: Decline core config and document host umask, ACL, group, or container-user setup as the supported operator path.

recommendation.title: Scoped opt-in policy
recommendation.body: Add a narrowly scoped user-output permission policy that applies only to approved agent-output paths and explicitly excludes OpenClaw private state.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses filesystem safety, config policy, and sandbox/apply_patch security boundaries where steipete has the strongest feature-history signal.
